items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Melba Liston is responsible for the arrangements.

ctx.x: How much music does he write out? Quite a bit of it? And you get the solo spot?

No. Well quite a bit for the form, but it doesn’t seem like much. Melba Liston is responsible for the arrangements. And I don’t know they’re really not extensive, not like a big band with an A, B, C and D. There will be a line here, a whole 16 bars or whatever, 32, and then there’ll be maybe a middle or a transition. But actually it’s built around the solos and stuff. The written music is for interludes or set-ups for the solos.
I was glad to see her name.

items.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: On your first one you had Bennie Green, Al Grey, Benny Powell.

ctx.x: How did the record date come up with Melba and her ’Bones. On your first one you had Bennie Green, Al Grey, Benny Powell.
